title: GSCore: Efficient Radiance Field Rendering via Architectural Support for 3D Gaussian Splatting
problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting rendering is computationally intensive, limiting deployment on resource-constrained devices like mobile GPUs. Efficient hardware support is needed to make this radiance field rendering technique practical for real-time applications.
motivation: 3D Gaussian Splatting offers powerful rendering quality but requires specialized hardware acceleration to achieve real-time performance on mobile and edge devices for widespread adoption.
method: GSCore integrates three algorithmic optimizations into a custom ASIC design synthesized in 28nm: Gaussian shape-aware intersection testing to determine which gaussians affect each pixel, hierarchical sorting to order gaussians efficiently for rendering, and subtile skipping to eliminate redundant computations in empty regions. These techniques are synergistically combined in the hardware pipeline.
key_novelty: Custom hardware architecture specifically designed for 3D Gaussian Splatting with shape-aware intersection testing, hierarchical sorting, and subtile skipping optimizations synergistically integrated into a single accelerator.
contributions: GSCore ASIC accelerator achieving 15.86× speedup with reduced area and energy versus mobile GPU
Gaussian shape-aware intersection test optimization for efficient pixel-gaussian interactions
Hierarchical sorting technique for optimal gaussian rendering order
Subtile skipping method to reduce redundant computations
primary_theme: Hardware acceleration for Gaussian Splatting rendering
